subject.title: feat(zalouser): recover accepted messages after local crashes

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this Zalo Personal crash-window durability contract—persisting accepted raw callbacks and retaining completion/failed tombstones—as the supported channel behavior?
rationale: The implementation changes user-visible inbound-delivery semantics and durable local state; repository policy treats channel delivery and persisted state as compatibility-sensitive, while the protected maintainer label requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Adopt with live recovery proof
options.body: Approve the owner-plugin design after a redacted real Zalo crash/restart run proves the stated acceptance-to-dispatch recovery boundary and the refreshed merge head is green.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep only the shared-queue integration if maintainers do not want the documented tombstone retention and replay behavior as a supported Zalo Personal contract.

options.title: Defer durability support
options.body: Pause the PR if Zalo Personal should remain best-effort until a broader channel-ingress persistence policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Adopt with live recovery proof
recommendation.body: Approve the owner-plugin design after a redacted real Zalo crash/restart run proves the stated acceptance-to-dispatch recovery boundary and the refreshed merge head is green.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned author owns the proposed ingress design and can clarify its intended Zalo delivery contract; additional current-main area ownership evidence was not available from the read-only inspection environment.
